name: Aghu Tharnggalu (Retired)
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: Retired ISO bookkeeping entry (gtu, split into gtu/ggm/ikr in 2013); no documentation of its own beyond aghu1254's.

sources.citation: English Wikipedia, 'Aghu Tharrnggala language' (wikitext downloaded 2026-09-17); phonology tables sourced to Jolly 1989.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Consonant and vowel charts only; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Verstraete, Jean-Christophe (2018). The genetic status of Lamalamic: phonological and morphological evidence. Oceanic Linguistics 57(1): 1-30 (ANU open-access postprint, hdl 1885/255113).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Uses Aghu Tharrnggala (Jolly 1989) as a neighbouring comparison language; fn. 13 cites Jolly 1989:25-30 on two doubtful fricatives; says nothing about Aghu Tharrnggala stress.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority (2012). Change Request 2012-138: split of [ggr] Aghu Tharnggalu into [gtu] Aghu-Tharnggala, [ggm] Gugu-Mini, [ikr] Ikarranggal (effective 2013-01-23). SIL International.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; administrative document establishing that gtu (= this bookkeeping key) denotes Aghu-Tharnggala proper after the split of ggr.

sources.citation: Blevins, Juliette (2001). Where have all the onsets gone? Initial consonant loss in Australian Aboriginal languages. In J. Simpson, D. Nash, M. Laughren, P. Austin & B. Alpher (eds), Forty years on: Ken Hale and Australian languages, 481-492. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics 512.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Survey of initial-dropping languages: lists the sister language Kuku-Thaypan among languages where 'stress has shifted from first to second syllable' with 'invariable' initial C-loss (source Rigsby 1976), but Aghu Tharrnggala is not mentioned anywhere in the paper.

sources.citation: Nash, David (2001). Bibliography of Ken Hale and Australian languages. In Simpson et al. (eds), Forty years on, 1-18. Pacific Linguistics 512.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; documents the primary materials: Hale 1960 'Aghu-Tharnggala (Hann R. Language)' field notes, speaker George Meldrum, Kalinga Stn, 36 l., 'vocabulary and elicitation; phonemes', AIATSIS MS 2200, tape A3163, transcribed by Rigsby (AIATSIS pMS 2326) and by Jolly 1989.

sources.citation: Glottolog languoid record aghu1254 (JSON) and Grambank CLDF (local copy: both cite Jolly 1989 (s_Jolly_Tharrnggala) as the sole description.

sources.note: Modern comparative treatment of Thaypanic (Kuku Thaypan, Aghu Tharrnggala) by a phonologically careful author; may state the shared prosodic profile (stress shift with initial-dropping) for the subgroup including Aghu Tharrnggala.
